notes.title: City Transport Simulator Bus + Tram - Update v1.2.2
notes.notes:
[h1]CTS Update v1.2.2 is here![/h1]

With version 1.2.2, City Transport Simulator receives a major update that noticeably improves immersion: signals have finally been adjusted so you’ll experience fewer delays. In addition, the update gives you new customization options for the stop chime, lets you transfer renamed stations to Sandbox Mode, and fixes numerous bugs.

For more info, check out our new video here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X_9japvTkM0

[h1]CTS v1.2.2 Changelog[/h1]

[h2]New Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Stop Chime[/b] can now be selected in the customization menu.
[*] [b]Flexity[/b]: Added camera and mirror adjustment.
[*] New [b]Indicator Off[/b] key binding available for buses.
[*] [b]Renamed Stations[/b] in Career Mode can now be [b]transferred to Sandbox Mode[/b].
[/list]

[h2]Improvements & Optimizations[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Signals reworked[/b] to significantly reduce waiting times.
[*] [b]Main Station[/b]: Adjusted speed limits.
[*] [b]Passenger system improved[/b]:

[list]
[*] Spawn only at stops with [b]actual departures[/b].
[*] Now check timetables and are assigned to a matching [b]line[/b].
[*] Players can easily walk [b]through passengers[/b] without getting stuck.
[/list]
[/list]

[h2]Vehicles[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]MAN Lion’s City[/b]:
[list]
[*] Fixed [b]artifacts and shading errors[/b] on the rear window.
[*] Removed [b]graphic glitch[/b] on the front destination display.
[*] Passengers now [b]board correctly[/b] at the starting position.
[*] Black exterior areas are now [b]properly glazed[/b].
[/list]
[*] [b]ECAS system[/b]: Improved kneeling function—no longer gets stuck, especially on articulated and double-axle buses.
[*] [b]MAN Lion’s City A23[/b] (3-door): Fixed double seat occupancy.
[*] [b]MAN Lion’s City A26/A47[/b]: Added mirror material at door 2.
[*] [b]E1[/b]: Line number now displays correctly.
[*] [b]R2.2b[/b]: Corrected cloudy window panes.
[*] [b]StadtRegioTram[/b]: Fixed mirror clipping when adjusting.
[*] [b]GT6[/b]: No penalty for deadman’s switch.
[*] [b]GT8N[/b]: Added vehicle length in selection menu.
[*] [b]ULF[/b]: Door release now reliably disengages the brake.
[*] [b]GT6[/b]: Added headlight beams.
[*] Adjusted [b]pantograph heights[/b].
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Switch rod[/b] functional again.
[*] [b]Collision detection with AI vehicles[/b] corrected.
[*] Fixed issue where [b]vehicles ran red lights[/b] at intersections.
[*] Added [b]missing overhead line[/b] at Jakob-De-Zuet-Straße.
[*] Correctly positioned [b]stop marker[/b] at Toriyama Allee.
[*] Fixed issue where [b]fewer passengers appeared over time[/b].
[*] [b]In-game hints[/b] no longer repeatedly appear/disappear.
[*] Fixed issue where [b]view angle couldn’t be changed[/b] after seat adjustment.
[*] Resolved issue where the [b]steering wheel became unresponsive[/b] if mouse mode was set to “throttle/brake only”.
[/list]

notes.title: City Transport Simulator - Roadmap July Update
notes.notes:
[h1]Welcome to the new roadmap for City Transport Simulator![/h1]
Since the release of [b]City Transport Simulator: Bus[/b], a lot has happened and we have received tons of feedback from you. Today, we are excited to finally present the new roadmap for City Transport Simulator!
In the coming months, you can expect not only bug fixes and small features but also real content highlights, new vehicles, expansions, and a look into the future of CTS.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/db300cb0ad5857b82dd4ce4d8991b47566b3d84b.jpg[/img]

[h2]Looking back at the launch of CTS: Bus[/h2]
In June, we released City Transport Simulator: Bus on Steam, making our vision of an all-in-one simulation a reality — a game where bus and tram traffic go hand in hand on a lively, constantly evolving map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/a0d1a6712d3d9fb207026f627935b01f84304e5c.png[/img]

But the release was just the beginning: just like with CTS: Tram, we plan long-term support with new content, major features, and of course integrating your feedback, which we’ve received in large amounts through Discord, Steam, and social media over the past weeks. Thank you for that!

[h2]Next update: Mouse control, improvements & more[/h2]
The next update is already on the horizon with one of the most requested features from you:

[b]Mouse control for buses[/b]
Using the ALT key or directly via the control settings, you will soon be able to steer your bus intuitively with the mouse — no gamepad or wheel required.

[b]Physics improvements for trams[/b]
The Flexity Vienna will get better acceleration on inclines, and the Munich R2.2b will have more realistic sinusoidal movement and swaying adjustments.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/5c7639fcff01ca8b019e0251d93b39e6842c5c5c.jpg[/img]

And after that, there will be more [b]updates[/b]:

[list]
[*] [b]AI and signal improvements[/b]
We continuously work on optimizing traffic lights, AI vehicles, and overall traffic dynamics.
[*] [b]More life inside vehicles[/b]
New passenger voices will add even more acoustic variety, plus new announcement voices in several languages including English, French, Polish, and Hungarian.
[/list]

[h2]More vehicles in the works![/h2]
Of course, we are also expanding the vehicle roster for CTS with real classics and more compact bus variants.

[h3][b]GT6 (Tram Classic):[/b][/h3]
The legendary articulated tram GT6 brings retro flair to Tramau. With its charming look, distinctive driving style, and historic interior, this vehicle is made for all nostalgia fans!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/b64ae654481642212404c3f23d933777e88c2992.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]MAN Lion’s City A47 & A26[/b][/h3]
With the [b]A47[/b] and [b]A26[/b], we expand the fleet with two exciting 10- and 15-meter variants of the MAN Lion’s City.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/b8fe441e6a068315b003576fbc5a609028cdb02e.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/140629555b5f56d4f918c16bb03cca65a5ad21d3.png[/img]

Both models bring fresh energy to your fleet and enable new deployment options! More info on release timing and features will follow in one of the upcoming updates.

[h2]Looking ahead: Autumn highlights & console release[/h2]
Autumn will bring the next big phase of CTS with a special focus on the [b]console release for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S[/b]. The game is already very advanced technically, and we are working closely with Sony and Microsoft to complete the final steps for launch.

[h2]Free map expansion for all Depot DLC owners[/h2]
With the big autumn release comes a comprehensive [b]free map expansion for everyone who owns the “Depot + Southern Lines” DLC[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/5f6f4cff1616f1e225f318f750bc420f0006eaf5.jpg[/img]

The new route takes you through a completely redesigned city district with [b]high-rise buildings and an urban metropolitan flair[/b]. In contrast to the previous districts in Tramau, here you will experience a completely different vibe: faster, denser, more hectic!

Additionally, the route is brought to life by [b]new AI passengers in business attire[/b] and a higher passenger density. People on their way to the office, appointments, or meetings. This gives the neighborhood a whole new atmosphere.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/84c9524dfbddb796e1898f93fefb06a9900320c5.jpg[/img]

[b]And do you remember the big construction site at the tram depot in the south of the map?[/b] That exact construction site will be transformed into a [b]new bus parking lot[/b] with this update! From now on, you’ll be able to [b]start or end your shifts as a bus driver in the south of the map as well[/b]. This not only brings more variety to your routes but also expands your daily itineraries and how you play the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/2d6e14d37317f33bd9722fd436f022bef7766444.jpg[/img]

The bus map expansion will be released [b]simultaneously with the console release in autumn 2025[/b] and is, as mentioned, free for all who already own the [b]Depot + Southern Lines DLC[/b]. If you don’t have the DLC yet, no problem: it remains available and offers a large tram depot, new stops, and a completely different route layout even without the expansion.

[h2]The MAN New Lion’s City 12C & 18C[/h2]
Many of you have wished for it — now it’s official: we are working on the [b]new generation of the MAN Lion’s City[/b]! With the 12C (solo bus) and 18C (articulated bus), we expand the City Transport Simulator fleet with a modern bus family that sets new standards in design and technology.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/25fe8ea61d5a9f7d3aab35de8e364a66dcc7d7e9.jpg[/img]

In collaboration with [b]VOR[/b] and [b]Dr. Richard[/b], we were again able to access original data and materials to recreate the bus as authentically as possible. From the paint job to the cockpit details — everything is being crafted with great attention to detail.

We are especially proud of the colorful LED interior lighting, which gives the vehicle a special flair and creates a unique atmosphere both day and night.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/b3bbfff0a6f6dedacb03bd59fb096c36c186eca8.jpg[/img]

Currently, the New Lion’s City is in [b]work-in-progress phase[/b]. This means we are actively working on the 3D model, driving physics, sounds, and interior design. We’re very happy about your feedback on the first images and do our best to incorporate your wishes into the fine-tuning.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/64b44faf4ac63bf662d06c4b1ddae54558b5c74d.jpg[/img]

The release of the New Lion’s City is planned together with the [b]big console release and free map expansion in autumn 2025[/b]. So you can look forward to a powerful overall package!

[h2]Roadmap Phase 3: Weather, tickets, new cities[/h2]
What comes after autumn? Here’s a glance at the third phase:

[list]
[*] 🌧️ [b]Dynamic weather[/b]: rain, lightning, temperature changes — including effects on driving behavior and climate control inside vehicles
[*] 🎫 [b]Ticket sales[/b]: realistic ticket selling on the bus
[*] 🚋 [b]Tatra KT4D[/b]: an old tram with special charm — currently in development
[*] 🚌 [b]New bus model[/b]: still a secret, but already planned
[*] 🏙️ [b]Vienna returns![/b]: new routes for bus & tram based on a new, improved routing system
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/db300cb0ad5857b82dd4ce4d8991b47566b3d84b.jpg[/img]

[b]City Transport Simulator[/b] is just getting started and thanks to your feedback, the simulation gets better, bigger, and more varied every month!

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Bus + Tram - Update 1.1.2
notes.notes:
[h1]CTS Update v1.1.2 is here – with Fixes, Features & Improvements[/h1]

Today’s update brings several bug fixes and features we’ve already talked about – many of them based directly on your feedback.

Some of the key changes include fixing crashes during game startup (e.g. caused by remapped keys), various reported issues with traffic lights and AI behavior, and the incorrect tram reset in Eglundsdorf.

In addition to those fixes, we’ve added a few highly requested features:

[list]
[*] You can now adjust the [b]Field of View (FOV)[/b]
[*] Steering [b]speed[/b] and [b]return-to-center speed[/b] are now individually configurable – for mouse & keyboard, gamepad/controller, and even steering wheels
[/list]

This gives you much more control over your gameplay experience!

We’ve also reworked the [b]MAN Lion’s City 3D model[/b] with great attention to detail. Thanks to your feedback, both the cockpit and passenger area are now much more realistic and accurate.

[h2]🔄 What’s next?[/h2]

Of course, we’re continuing to improve the game with your help. We're currently working on:
[list]
[*] A new [b]mouse steering[/b] mode
[*] Improvements to [b]trams[/b], especially the Flexity and R2.2b models
[*] [b]Better AI behavior[/b]: We’re aware that cars sometimes ignore red lights or right-of-way rules – this is a top priority for upcoming updates
[/list]

[h2]📋 Changelog v1.1.2[/h2]

[h3]Features[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added FOV setting
[*] Added AI bus lines for tram module
[*] New settings for steering and return speeds (mouse, gamepad, wheel)
[*] Bus and tram lines in sandbox mode can now be restored separately
[/list]

[h3]Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Vienna IBIS destination entries (1, 2) now work correctly

[h3]AI & Collisions[/h3]

[h3]Vehicles[/h3]

[*] Door release could be activated while driving – fixed
[*] Added in-game hint if doors 1 and 2 aren’t opened (Lion’s City A21 T2)

[/list]

[h3]MAN Lion’s City 3D Model Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added floor hatches under rear seats

[*] Added heating strips on cockpit window
[*] Relocated stop request buttons
[*] Door mechanism now centered

notes.notes:
[h1]City Transport Simulator: Bus + Tram Update v1.1.1 Now Live[/h1]

[b]City Transport Simulator: Tram[/b] just got a major update! With version 1.1.1, we're bringing over 50 new missions, stop platform choice, visual upgrades, many fixed and more AI interactions to enrich your experience. Plus, we're excited to announce that City Transport Simulator: Bus is officially out now and available on Steam!

[h2]Changelog[/h2]

[b]New Content and Features[/b]
[list]
[*] 50 brand-new missions available across both modules
[*] 8 new sandbox lines added for buses
[*] Basic Bus Tutorial introduced for first-time drivers and also available in CTS: Tram
[*] Bus Map Extension added for AI buses in CTS: Tram and for CTS: Bus
[*] Station names are now editable in the Operations Menu
[*] Berlin, Munich, and Vienna-style station elements can now be switched in the Personalization Menu
[*] Line creation now allows choosing the platform for more flexible endstation usage
[*] New main menu design and updated loading screen key art
[/list]

[b]Gameplay and AI Enhancements[/b]
[list]
[*] Passengers now greet you when boarding and react to your driving style
[*] AI cars now honk in response to reckless driving
[*] No collision timer for low-speed collisions with cars
[/list]

[b]Visual and UX Improvements[/b]
[list]
[*] Lighting system upgraded to Lumen for enhanced visual fidelity
[*] Mirror resolution increased
[*] Shadows under trams improved
[*] Traffic light cycles reworked
[*] Ground markings added and improved across the map
[*] Stop markers at stations now align with guidance strips for the visually impaired
[*] HUD stop marker for trams changed to a semi-cylinder
[/list]

[b]Controls and Settings[/b]
[list]
[*] Steering wheel support added (see Control Settings)
[*] Force Feedback options for CTS: Bus now available in Gameplay Settings
[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed AI car driving into tram at Sommerfeldgarten
[*] Fixed E1 tram driving too fast
[*] Fixed crash when entering line 0 in Vienna IBIS
[/list]

[h2]Known Issues[/h2]
[list]
[*] Career mode bus lines are not automatically added for existing players of CTS: Tram, which causes AI buses to not appear in career mode when using an existing save.
[*] Sandbox mode bus lines are also not automatically added for existing players of CTS: Tram. You’ll need to press “Restore Default Lines” — but please note that this will delete any custom sandbox lines you’ve created.
[/list]
We are actively working on fixing these two issues and will provide a hotfix as soon as possible, so that CTS: Tram players can experience AI buses as promised. Thank you for your patience!

[h2]Thanks for Your Support![/h2]

This update reflects a lot of your feedback, and we’re incredibly grateful for your patience and passion as we continue building City Transport Simulator together.

We’re just getting started — more improvements and features are on the way. In the meantime, enjoy the new missions, customizable stations, improved AI, and everything CTS: Bus has to offer.

notes.title: Thank you for your Feedback about Update v1.0.3!
notes.notes:
Thank you for your great feedback on the new version 1.0.3 of City Transport Simulator: Tram!

If you don't have CTS: Tram yet, the Collector's Edition is currently 20% off until March 20! Get it now in the Steam Spring Sale: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2604480/City_Transport_Simulator_Tram/

Here’s a look at our upcoming plans:

[h2]🔹 More Frequent Updates[/h2]  
We have optimized our development and testing processes, allowing us to release updates more quickly and regularly—sometimes as frequently as every 2–3 weeks!  
To ensure the quality of these updates, we have carefully selected dedicated players from our community as beta testers. These testers get early access to new versions and help us detect bugs and test improvements. Their feedback has already contributed significantly to optimizations!  
If you haven’t already, join our Discord: https://discord.gg/ZqFJeTQS  

[h2]🔹 Adjustment of Tram Signal Phases[/h2]  
With update 1.0.3, we have reworked the signaling system to create more realistic traffic light phases. However, this has also resulted in trams sometimes having to wait too long. We are actively working on adjusting the signal timings and line schedules to make the process smoother—without making the simulation too easy. 😉  

[h2]🔹 Improved Driving Physics for the R2.2b[/h2]  
The sinusoidal movement of the R2.2b tram is currently being adjusted! This will reduce lateral swaying in curves and even on straight tracks, making the driving experience even more realistic.  

[h2]🔹 Performance Optimizations & Crash Fixes for Xbox Series X/S[/h2]  
Some of you have reported performance issues and crashes, especially on Xbox Series S. In the upcoming updates, we are optimizing roads, sidewalks, and trams to prevent crashes and improve overall performance—benefiting all platforms!  

[h2]🔹 Announcements for Xbox Series X/S[/h2]  
We recently received an update for the announcements plugin on Xbox Series X/S, but there are still technical issues. The plugin developer is already working on a fix, and as soon as the feature is stable, we will release a hotfix so you can use announcements as soon as possible.  

[h2]🔹 New Navigation System[/h2]  
The previous HUD navigation didn’t meet our expectations. In the next update, you can expect a dynamic navigation system that will guide you directly through the city. You can choose between different display styles: the full route, short distances, or only switch points. Check out our latest ViewApp Insights for a first look: https://youtu.be/5pOy5Nr8apE?feature=shared  

Thank you for your support! 🚋

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram - Roadmap February Update
notes.notes:
[h1]A Glimpse into the Future of City Transport Simulator[/h1]  

First of all, we would like to sincerely thank you for the great launch of [b]City Transport Simulator: Tram[/b]! Your support and constructive feedback mean the world to us. It shows that what we are building together has a strong and engaged player base behind it.

Of course, not everything went perfectly, and some issues have affected your gameplay experience. That's why today, we want to be transparent with you about what we're currently working on and what is planned for [b]City Transport Simulator[/b] in the near and distant future.

[h2]Stability and Bug Fixes[/h2]  

The first week was intense. We've been closely monitoring your feedback and are working hard on an update that will address the most reported issues. Right now, the focus is on crashes, especially those related to the [b]E1 tram model[/b] – both the player and AI versions.

[b]In the next patch, you can expect:[/b]  
- Fix for AI E1 trams getting stuck in traffic  
- Fix for crashes related to the E1  
- Fix for crashes on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S & PC  
- Corrections to the target and line display on the GT8N and E1  

Another important point is the [b]missing station announcements on consoles[/b]. Unfortunately, we still have to wait for an update to the plugin that handles these annotuncements, which will cause a slight delay. But rest assured, we will deliver the announcements as soon as we can. Since the crash fixes are a higher priority, we don’t want you to wait any longer for those.

[h2]AI Improvements, Feedback, and Dynamic Weather[/h2]  

The [b]optimization of the vehicle and passenger AI[/b] remains a central focus, particularly when it comes to realistic priority rules and smoother traffic flow. We also continue to pay attention to your feedback, which is why we are currently working on a [b]free track selection[/b] at certain termini when creating lines. The goal is to avoid traffic jams and make the simulation even more realistic together with improvements in tram AI.

Of course, [b]dynamic weather[/b] is still a major focus. Since we want to implement realistic effects such as changed driving behavior, functional windshield wipers, and heating, as well as adjusted passenger behavior, this feature will take a bit longer.

What is nearly finished, however, is the [b]fully customizable controls[/b]. We know that everyone has their own preferences when it comes to control settings, which is why you will soon be able to reassign all the relevant keys and functions for both keyboard and gamepad. Additional improvements for joystick configuration will also be coming.

[h2]What’s Next?[/h2]  

We want to give you more ways to personalize your gameplay experience in the future. Soon, you'll be able to not only [b]set custom names for stations[/b], but also give the city itself a name of your choice.

This is an important step in further enhancing immersion and turning your city into a personal, unique game world. We're also working on offering [b]station announcements in more languages[/b], making the experience even more authentic and international.

Additionally, we want to give you the ability to [b]customize the appearance of your stops[/b]. With different presets, inspired by [b]real cities[/b], your city's look will become more varied and lively.

[h2]Navigation and City Design[/h2]  

A major point of feedback was the [b]minimap[/b], which at times caused more confusion than help. Therefore, we are working on a new solution, similar to the green circles at the stations, that will guide you naturally through the city without being intrusive.

There will also be some changes to the map itself. In addition to further improvements to switches and signals, we plan to expand and decorate many of the inner-city streets to make the city even more immersive.

[h2]New Vehicles and Surprises[/h2]  

Yes, new vehicles are still planned! Which ones exactly will be kept a surprise for now, but we’re sure you won’t expect some of the models coming your way.

Thank you for your support and feedback. We look forward to continuing to work on [b]City Transport Simulator[/b] with you!

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram - Beta Update v0.4.0 now out!
notes.notes:
[h1]Beta Update v0.4.0 – New Features, Improvements, and Bug Fixes[/h1]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wW0o-krU3_k

We are excited to announce the release of Beta Update 0.4.0 for City Transport Simulator: Tram! This update brings a number of exciting new features, important improvements, and bug fixes that enhance the overall gameplay experience. 

Attention: Please note that the beta update is optional and can currently lead to many crashes. It can also happen that the new storage system can cause the save data in the experimental update to be lost (but it will still be retained in the stable update!)

Here are the key changes:

[h2]New Features[/h2]
- Joystick support: You can now experience the game with joysticks and take full control!
- Two new map extensions: 6 new stations (including 2 terminal stations) with an old town atmosphere and grass tracks
- Controller preset: We’ve added predefined controller settings to get you started right away.
- Keyboard preset: New keyboard settings offer an improved control experience.
- Keychain collectible available: Collect the new item and expand your in-game collection!

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
- Intersection at Stadtgraben: We’ve fixed an issue where cars at the intersection in Stadtgraben weren’t moving – everything is running smoothly now!
- Cockpit Legend achievement: The Cockpit Legend achievement now works as intended, so no more worries during your pursuit of achievements!
- Overall satisfaction: A general satisfaction of 5.0 is now possible again – meaning you can achieve even better results in the simulation!

[h2]Improvements[/h2]
- Upgrade to UE5.4: The game has been updated to the latest version of Unreal Engine 5.4, improving performance and stability.
- Hauptbahnhof through station: The Hauptbahnhof now features a through station – a perfect addition for your daily routes!
- Schmiedegasse advance signals: Advance signals are now present in Schmiedegasse, making the traffic situation even more realistic.

Beta Update 0.4.0 is now available for testing! We look forward to your feedback and continuing to improve the game. Have fun playing!

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram Update 0.4.0 and 1.0 Release Date
notes.notes:
[h1]Update 0.4.0: Joystick Support and New Map Expansions[/h1]

[h2]Joystick Support and Customisable Controls[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/81641ee4ceed2b8f1ac0d44359da138d208876e1.png[/img]

One of the most popular community requests is going to be released into the beta branch in the near future! With Update 0.4.0, players can look forward to joystick support and customisable controls. This update will introduce new presets for keyboard and controller inputs, giving players more flexibility and precision as they navigate the city of Tramau.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/c9ba17490fb18c366cc9601a2d7b71a3990f0c49.png[/img]

Update 0.4.0 will also bring two exciting map expansions designed to enhance Tramau’s unique old-town atmosphere. In these new areas, players will experience the city without the usual car traffic, immersing themselves in Tramau’s historic charm. One of the standout features of these expansions is the addition of grass tracks, which not only offer a beautiful aesthetic but also provide a fresh feel to the tram-driving experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/9131373e32b9e9fd31aa6e1b46a9de58858cfa65.png[/img]

An additional highlight is the inclusion of a construction site at one of the stations, adding an extra layer of engagement and showing the evolving nature of Tramau’s cityscape. Together, these expansions offer deeper immersion, allowing players to explore the peaceful old town as well as newer, underutilised areas of the city.

After a successful run in Early Access, we're thrilled to announce the full 1.0 release of City Transport Simulator: Tram for PC on January 28th, 2025! This marks a major milestone for the game, delivering the complete tram-driving experience that players have been eagerly awaiting.

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram - Roadmap November Update!
notes.notes:
Welcome to the new CTS: Tram Roadmap Update! Since our last roadmap update, a lot has happened in City Transport Simulator: Tram. We're excited to bring you up to date and share a look ahead at the upcoming improvements and features coming your way in the next few months.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/891670a561b0cc93c879ea41e1cb7b82f199ef94.jpg[/img]

[h2]A Look Back at v0.3.0 and v0.3.1[/h2]

With Update v0.3.0, we introduced major expansions and officially completed Phase 1. We added important content like the Vienna Tram Type D, new career mode levels, and a variety of liveries.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/d3254d9211250f3b63a07dd0128c4b3dccb0ff8e.jpg[/img]

We also expanded the map with a siding track, giving you the option to start as a special service train or finish your route there. To make the gameplay experience more dynamic, we updated the loading screen gallery and added AI trains at the main station to bring the world of Tramau even more to life.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/da64dd6db1c73f6579e0243d8db8ea4ca7c74f33.jpg[/img]

The latest update, v0.3.1, marked the beginning of Phase 2. In this phase, we focused primarily on optimizing AI behavior, switches, and signals, along with fixing numerous bugs reported by you. Additionally, we increased the variety of street traffic and passengers to create an even more immersive game world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/1904243d8f70fc38bce1128edbaff9b773795130.jpg[/img]

[h2]New Update in the Works – v0.3.2[/h2]

Your feedback is incredibly important to us, and based on that, we’re focusing primarily on bug fixes and stability improvements for v0.3.2. We take your reports on Discord and the Steam Forum seriously and are working to create an even more solid gameplay experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/55f4d76d7275d16b03a2dfe4ff6c6e14158ff1cf.jpg[/img]

However, we will be adding a brand-new feature: collectible keychains! Similar to the postcards you know, you’ll now be able to find souvenir machines around the city that offer keychains.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/af8ca3acf9417bf0da62a4ddc6fd6eae53da2d2a.jpg[/img]

Each keychain features a tram and includes fascinating background information about that particular tram model—perfect for those who want to get to know the vehicles outside of their daily routes!

[h2]The Roadmap – A Look Ahead[/h2]

Our roadmap offers you a clear overview of what to expect in upcoming updates. It gives you a taste of the features and expansions that are on the way.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/891670a561b0cc93c879ea41e1cb7b82f199ef94.jpg[/img]

[h3]Joystick Support and Customizable Controls[/h3]

We know how important joystick support is to many of you. That’s why we’re working hard on providing joystick and presets for keyboard and controller. Although this feature has been delayed slightly, you can look forward to enjoying it in CTS: Tram later this year!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/81641ee4ceed2b8f1ac0d44359da138d208876e1.png[/img]  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/39eb6bd6e8c45c8363fa165a4ddcca786f60d841.png[/img]

[h3]Two Planned Map Expansions[/h3]

These new expansions are designed specifically to enhance the unique old town feel. In the old town areas, the atmosphere of Tramau really comes alive—without the usual car traffic that shapes the cityscape elsewhere.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/60655b8915ab5f4328178044ef63f9fd4396dc73.png[/img]

Another highlight of this expansion is the grass tracks, which not only enhance the aesthetic but also give the route a different feel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/1c346dafdf1949f07afe370a3201b3c7ee562789.png[/img]

We’ve also added an interesting construction site at one station, providing an engaging change of pace and allowing you to experience the ever-evolving city landscape.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/9131373e32b9e9fd31aa6e1b46a9de58858cfa65.png[/img]

Overall, these expansions not only provide a deeper immersion into the world of Tramau, but also deliver a varied gameplay experience, allowing you to explore both the tranquil old town and the city’s new, underutilized areas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/0a9f4f5bff3f9e6c8cfe1f307210fdf9a40ac0c9.jpg[/img]

[h2]The Path to Console Release[/h2]

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram – Dev Diary Update #1
notes.notes:
[h1]City Transport Simulator: Tram – Dev Diary Update #1[/h1]

Hello everyone,
We are excited to give you a deeper insight into the latest developments and improvements for City Transport Simulator: Tram. Due to the high demand from the community, we have decided to publish this Dev Diary to highlight some of the most important changes and bug fixes.

You can watch the video version of our Dev Diary here (only available in German): https://youtu.be/TrTk1GDnDEA

[h1]Overview: Recent Changes and Improvements[/h1]

In recent weeks, we have been working intensively to stabilize and optimize the gameplay experience in CTS: Tram. We are currently in an intensive testing phase of a new version of the game. We are working on testing and fixing the remaining bugs before we release the update.

[h2]New Gameplay Options[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/8e25555b3d73aaabb5ccc10b2b8613b3118ab7de.jpg[/img]

Some changes we've already implemented include new options that give players more control, such as:

[*] [b]Green Stop Markers:[/b] These can now be toggled on or off.
[*] [b]Tram Braking Power Adjustment:[/b] This option was added specifically for the "Type D" tram, which now has stronger braking power.
[*] [b]AI Density:[/b] The density of AI cars and pedestrians can now be set to "low," "medium," or "high." This improves the game’s adaptability to different performance configurations.

[h2]Improved AI Pedestrians and Vehicle Behavior[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/fcaa3bb49e45a13a1d60307d6cfe6e0a9ce49ad1.jpg[/img]

One of our focuses in the past weeks has been improving the behavior of AI vehicles and pedestrians. Here's an overview of the changes:

[*] [b]Traffic Lights and Pedestrians:[/b] Pedestrians now behave more realistically at traffic lights, no longer crossing on red, and respecting traffic rules.
[*] [b]AI Trams:[/b] AI trams now stop properly to allow passengers to board and disembark and no longer get stuck on the tracks.
[*] [b]Optimized Vehicle and Passenger Spawning:[/b] The spawn logic has been revised so that vehicles and passengers are now integrated more efficiently and realistically into the game without negatively impacting performance.

[h2]Gameplay Adjustments[/h2]

There are also gameplay improvements:

[*] [b]Green Markers:[/b] These now work as they should, accurately indicating when and where to make the perfect stop.
[*] [b]Distance Display:[/b] The HUD now accurately shows the distance to the next stop after being revised.
[*] [b]Collision Logic Adjusted:[/b] Collisions now occur more realistically and at the correct times—whether between trams, cars, or pedestrians.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/06347d73f2accb99dacdd9fab0be378bb72c21ac.jpg[/img]

[h2]Switches and Signals[/h2]

Another major update concerned the functioning of the switches and signals in the game.

All the signals you encounter in the game now work correctly and are respected by both your tram and AI vehicles. As a result, there are no longer any issues with trams running red lights or unexpectedly stopping.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/9689bc742ef0bc0ecde3d26f0bd131d24db2f8e9.jpg[/img]

Bugs related to switches have also been removed. The automatic switch recognition and control now work as intended, contributing to smoother gameplay.

[h1]Recap of Update 0.3.0 and What's Next[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/d3254d9211250f3b63a07dd0128c4b3dccb0ff8e.jpg[/img]

In the last update (version 0.3.0), we added many new features like the Type D tram, a map expansion, and over 100 new loading screens to enrich the game experience.

With the upcoming update 0.3.1, we will primarily focus on bug fixes and improvements. While there will be no new features, the update will deliver a more stable and immersive gameplay experience.

[h2]Console Versions[/h2]

Another major focus is the work on the console versions for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S. Particularly for the Xbox Series S, it’s been a challenge to achieve optimal performance without simply reducing graphics quality and AI density.

We are working on ensuring that the game runs on consoles at medium graphics settings with stable 60 FPS. These improvements will also benefit the PC version.

[h2]What’s Coming Next?[/h2]

In the coming weeks, our focus will be on thorough testing. We want to make sure all systems are working flawlessly before releasing the update. Since quality is our top priority, there is no exact release date for the update yet, but we are planning to roll it out within the next few weeks.

We are very pleased with the progress we've made and are looking forward to delivering Update 0.3.1 to you soon.

It’s important to us that the game runs smoothly and stably for all players—whether on PC or console. That’s why we are taking the time to test everything thoroughly.

Thank you for your patience and support! We’ll keep you updated and are eager to hear your feedback.

Stay tuned—there’s much more to come!

notes.title: Status Update: Progress and Improvements - CTS: Tram
notes.notes:
[h1]Dear CTS: Tram Players,[/h1]

First of all, we sincerely apologize for the silence over the past few weeks. After the Dovetail Direct and the holiday period, some internal matters came up that unfortunately prevented us from responding to your requests more quickly. But from now on, we will be more active in engaging with the community and addressing all support tickets.

We want to assure you: Your messages are reaching us, and we hear you. Internally, we've had many discussions as we are just as dissatisfied with the quality of the v0.3.0 update as you are. This huge update was supposed to address several of your requests, but unfortunately, errors crept in that should not have happened – and we take full responsibility for that.

[h2]What are we doing now?[/h2]
Our first priority is to revise our internal processes. As you may have noticed, we are taking more time than usual for the next update. The reason for this is that we want to make this update as stable as possible. We are focusing heavily on bug fixes and gameplay balancing to finally resolve issues like malfunctioning traffic lights, stations, switches, or AI trams. Additionally, we are improving our QA process and investing more time in testing to identify and fix errors earlier, before the update is released.

[h2]What does this mean for you?[/h2]
There will be delays with the next update. We will keep you regularly updated via our Steam page, social media channels and community Discord and inform you exactly about the progress and current status of the update.

[h2]What can you expect in the next update?[/h2]
We are focusing primarily on bug fixes and stability, so there won’t be any major new features. However, these improvements are coming:

[h3]AI Behavior[/h3]
- Passengers will no longer be stuck in the ground.
- AI trams will follow their correct routes and no longer stop unexpectedly.
- AI trams will no longer pass through player trams.
- Collisions with vehicles and pedestrians will be more realistic and won’t trigger too early.

[h3]Signals & Switches[/h3]
- All switches will function correctly and can be operated either automatically or manually.
- All (switch) signals will work correctly.
- Traffic light phases will be realistically and correctly timed.
- Warnings like "Signal Ignored" will only appear after actually passing the signal.

[h3]Stations[/h3]
- Green stop markers will always be displayed correctly and can be disabled in the settings.
- All stops will appear correctly on the map.
- The "Missed Stop" warning will only show up if the stop was actually missed.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
- Tram brake force can now be customized in the settings.
- Speed limits are displayed correctly.


At the same time, we are continuing to work on the [b]PS5 and Xbox Series X/S versions[/b] of CTS: Tram. We’ll be able to share more details on the console version in October and possibly even announce a release date.

We hope you understand that we are working hard on addressing these issues and doing our best to ensure that something like this doesn’t happen again in the future. City Transport Simulator is just as important to us as it is to you, and we are committed to delivering a high-quality and enjoyable simulation based on your feedback. Your player experience is our top priority, and we will continue to do everything we can to improve it continuously.

Thank you for your patience and support!

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram - Early Access Roadmap Update!
notes.notes:
Welcome to the CTS: Tram Early Access Roadmap Update for July!

We have exciting news for you! Last week, we released a new update for City Transport Simulator: Tram. Early Access Version 0.1.3 includes several bug fixes based on your feedback from Discord and Steam. We have addressed issues with switches and graphic errors in R2.2b. Additionally, the ULF now operates as an AI tram in the city, and the stop announcements have been updated to "Next Stop" as requested by the community.

Unfortunately, the latest update also introduced a bug. If you start a session with the R2.2b in the evening or at night, the game might crash when the door opens. We are already working on a fix and will release it soon.

However, there’s a major update coming up that not only includes bug fixes but also introduces new features.

[h1]Version 0.2.0: New Features and Improvements[/h1]

We are excited to present all the details about City Transport Simulator: Tram Early Access Version 0.2.0! In addition to several bug fixes, this update will bring new features.

[h2]Quickplay Feature in Sandbox Mode[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/d7c3cdc5938c606a4aa04dff21d25698091c5394.png[/img]

You will finally be able to use the Quickplay feature in Sandbox Mode! This feature will generate a session with just one click, allowing you to start immediately. All lines, vehicles, and start times you’ve created in your Sandbox network will be randomly selected to quickly play any session.

[h2]Collectibles: Postcards[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/2c7f513022f677ec80618527e61039d74c0475e4.png[/img]

In Version 0.2.0, you will also receive the first collectible items: beautifully designed postcards that you can find throughout Tramau. You just need to locate the large postcard dispensers at specific landmarks to unlock a postcard. Each postcard will provide background stories about the landmarks, allowing you to dive deeper into Tramau.

[h2]First Map Expansion[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/d3e12cb1734ea8d20b36749b46b7060d696fdc5d.png[/img]

Version 0.2.0 will also introduce the first map expansion! Although initially planned for the second phase of Early Access, it’s ready earlier than expected. This update will add three new stations, including one end station. The southwestern part of the Tramau network will be expanded, creating new connections to the stations Amtsstraße, Friedlandstraße, and Igor-Yurkevic-Platz, providing more variety in your network.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/0529ec6440fd03d2d5a401adbee9028c3028c427.png[/img]

[h2]Updated Early Access Roadmap[/h2]

With this new update, we are also excited to show you the updated Early Access Roadmap. Based on your feedback and requests, we have added several new points. In addition to the map expansion coming in the next update, we will also introduce new liveries for all trams, which you can immediately use in Sandbox Mode and unlock progressively in Career Mode. We’ve come up with some really cool and also funny alternative liveries that we think you’ll love.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/b5603c4492e3a326823b21ea0e3d6ebcb7f225ed.jpg[/img]

[h2]Joystick Support and Further Updates[/h2]

In the first phase of our Early Access Roadmap, we have also added support for alternative controls for mouse & keyboard and controllers. Many of you have requested controls similar to TramSim and Train Sim World, which you will be able to select.

This is just the first phase of our control expansions. In the second phase, you will finally be able to use joysticks in City Transport Simulator: Tram. We are currently working on this functionality, which will take some time, so this feature is scheduled for the second phase of our Roadmap. Additionally, we plan to offer fully customizable key bindings. You will be able to assign any key on your keyboard or button on your controller to suit your preferred control setup.

[h2]Dovetail Direct Event[/h2]

We’ve already provided you with information about new updates and the updated Early Access Roadmap. But that’s not all! Our publisher Dovetail recently announced another Dovetail Direct Event on August 20th, and we will, of course, be participating with CTS: Tram.
